claim: Trypanosoma cruzi is the causative agent of Chagas disease.
source: The ability of the Chagas disease agent Trypanosoma cruzi to resist extended in vivo exposure to highly effective trypanocidal compounds prompted us to explore the potential for dormancy and its contribution to failed drug treatments in this infection.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established context for the study.

claim: Non-proliferating intracellular amastigotes develop in vivo in the absence of drug treatment.
source: We document the development of non-proliferating intracellular amastigotes in vivo and in vitro in the absence of drug treatment.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Non-proliferating intracellular amastigotes develop in vitro in the absence of drug treatment.
source: We document the development of non-proliferating intracellular amastigotes in vivo and in vitro in the absence of drug treatment.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Non-proliferative amastigotes convert to trypomastigotes.
source: Non-proliferative amastigotes ultimately converted to trypomastigotes and established infections in new host cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated experimentally in the results section.

claim: Non-proliferative amastigotes establish infections in new host cells.
source: Non-proliferative amastigotes ultimately converted to trypomastigotes and established infections in new host cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated experimentally in the results section.

claim: Dormant amastigotes are uniquely resistant to extended drug treatment in vivo.
source: Most significantly, dormant amastigotes were uniquely resistant to extended drug treatment in vivo and in vitro and could re-establish a flourishing infection after as many as 30 days of drug exposure.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: Dormant amastigotes are uniquely resistant to extended drug treatment in vitro.
source: Most significantly, dormant amastigotes were uniquely resistant to extended drug treatment in vivo and in vitro and could re-establish a flourishing infection after as many as 30 days of drug exposure.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 7.

claim: Dormant amastigotes can re-establish infection after 30 days of drug exposure.
source: Most significantly, dormant amastigotes were uniquely resistant to extended drug treatment in vivo and in vitro and could re-establish a flourishing infection after as many as 30 days of drug exposure.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 7.

claim: Dormancy in T. cruzi accounts for the failure of highly cytotoxic compounds to completely resolve infection.
source: These results demonstrate a dormancy state in T. cruzi that accounts for the failure of highly cytotoxic compounds to completely resolve the infection.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: T. cruzi infection in humans is relatively rarely treated.
source: Despite being one of the highest impact infectious diseases in the Americas, T. cruzi infection in humans is relatively rarely treated.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background information.

claim: Chagas disease was initially misconceived as having an autoimmune etiology rather than pathogen persistence.
source: Initially this was because of the misconception that Chagas disease had an autoimmune, rather than pathogen persistence etiology (Tarleton, 2003)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Benznidazole and nifurtimox have substantial toxic side effects.
source: but more recently the substantial toxic side effects and the limited supply of benznidazole (BZN) and nifurtimox (NFX), drugs that have been in use for decades, has also contributed significantly to their low rate of utilization.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background information.

claim: Treatment outcomes with benznidazole and nifurtimox range from 0% to 100% depending on the study.
source: However, the highly variable outcome of treatment regimens employing these compounds – ranging from 0% to 100% depending on the study - and the difficulty of accurately assessing these outcomes, also keep utilization as low as 1% of those infected (de Castro et al., 2006; Guedes et al., 2011; Jackson et al., 2010; Navarro et al., 2012; Yun et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations supporting the claim.

claim: Utilization of benznidazole and nifurtimox is as low as 1% of those infected.
source: However, the highly variable outcome of treatment regimens employing these compounds – ranging from 0% to 100% depending on the study - and the difficulty of accurately assessing these outcomes, also keep utilization as low as 1% of those infected (de Castro et al., 2006; Guedes et al., 2011; Jackson et al., 2010; Navarro et al., 2012; Yun et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: The high variability in efficacy of BZN and NFX has been primarily attributed to the broad genetic diversity of T. cruzi isolates.
source: The reason for the high variability in the efficacy of BZN and NFX is not known but has been primarily attributed to the broad genetic diversity of T. cruzi isolates.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a commonly held view.

claim: Lack of drug efficacy is almost certainly not a result of selection of genetic resistance by drug use or misuse.
source: Importantly, the lack of drug efficacy is almost certainly not a result of selection of genetic resistance by drug use or misuse, as neither BZN nor NFX have been widely or indiscriminately used and the induction of stable resistance to these drugs is difficult to produce in vitro or in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference based on drug usage patterns and experimental observations.

claim: Neither BZN nor NFX have been widely or indiscriminately used.
source: Importantly, the lack of drug efficacy is almost certainly not a result of selection of genetic resistance by drug use or misuse, as neither BZN nor NFX have been widely or indiscriminately used and the induction of stable resistance to these drugs is difficult to produce in vitro or in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background information.

claim: Induction of stable resistance to BZN and NFX is difficult to produce in vitro or in vivo.
source: Importantly, the lack of drug efficacy is almost certainly not a result of selection of genetic resistance by drug use or misuse, as neither BZN nor NFX have been widely or indiscriminately used and the induction of stable resistance to these drugs is difficult to produce in vitro or in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background information.

claim: Many T. cruzi infections in insects originate from feeding on non-human mammals.
source: Further, the variable and often low contribution of humans to infection of insect vectors (many infections in insects originate from feeding on non-human mammals, within which T. cruzi circulates widely and at high levels [Cohen and Gürtler, 2001]), offers very few opportunities to drive and spread resistance even if it were to develop.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: In bacterial infections, 'persister' cells develop that are transiently unaffected by chemotherapy due to metabolic dormancy.
source: In addition to classical genetic-based drug resistance, it has become increasingly appreciated that in bacterial infections, 'persister' cells develop that are transiently unaffected by chemotherapy, due in most cases to metabolic dormancy (reviewed in [Harms et al., 2016]).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to a review article.

claim: Bacterial persisters can arise spontaneously in the presence or absence of stress signals.
source: Such persisters can arise spontaneously in the presence or absence of stress signals and can reemerge after the termination of environmental challenges – such as antibiotic treatment.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background information about bacterial persisters.

claim: Bacterial persisters can reemerge after the termination of environmental challenges such as antibiotic treatment.
source: Such persisters can arise spontaneously in the presence or absence of stress signals and can reemerge after the termination of environmental challenges – such as antibiotic treatment.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background information about bacterial persisters.

claim: T. cruzi exhibits a biphasic kill curve with rapid death of most parasites but persistence of transiently non-replicating intracellular parasites.
source: We show that both in vitro and in vivo, T. cruzi exhibits a biphasic kill curve, with the rapid death of most parasites but the persistence of transiently non-replicating intracellular parasites that are resistant to high level and prolonged drug exposure.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a summary of the study's findings.

claim: BZN and NFX are normally dosed in animals (including humans) for 30–60 days.
source: The anti-T. cruzi drugs BZN and NFX are normally dosed in animals (including humans) for 30–60 days, although shorter treatment times can occasionally be curative (Bustamante et al., 2014; Viotti et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Shorter treatment times with BZN and NFX can occasionally be curative.
source: The anti-T. cruzi drugs BZN and NFX are normally dosed in animals (including humans) for 30–60 days, although shorter treatment times can occasionally be curative (Bustamante et al., 2014; Viotti et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations supporting the claim.

claim: A single oral dose of BZN reduced intracellular amastigotes at the initial infection site by ~90% within 48 hr.
source: Administration of a single oral dose of BZN reduced intracellular amastigotes at the initial infection site by ~90% within 48 hr (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: A rapid reduction in parasite load occurs in mice with established systemic infections within a few days after the initiation of oral BZN treatment.
source: A similarly rapid reduction in parasite load occurs in mice with established systemic infections within a few days after the initiation of oral BZN treatment (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: The colombiana and ARC-0704 T. cruzi strains were previously determined to be relatively more resistant to BZN in vivo.
source: In this later experiment we used multiple T. cruzi isolates, including two (colombiana and ARC-0704) previously determined to be relatively more resistant to BZN in vivo (Bustamante et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: The rate of parasite clearance was similar for all three strains (colombiana, ARC-0704, and CL-3).
source: The rate of parasite clearance, approaching the limit of detection by imaging, was similar for all three strains and in the case of the colombiana infection, the 5 days of treatment resulted in a > 3 log10 reduction in systemic parasite load.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: 5 days of BZN treatment resulted in a > 3 log10 reduction in systemic parasite load for colombiana infection.
source: The rate of parasite clearance, approaching the limit of detection by imaging, was similar for all three strains and in the case of the colombiana infection, the 5 days of treatment resulted in a > 3 log10 reduction in systemic parasite load.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: BZN rapidly and highly effectively kills both 'resistant' and 'susceptible' T. cruzi strains in vivo.
source: Thus, consistent with previous in vitro assessments, BZN rapidly and highly effectively kills both 'resistant' and 'susceptible' T. cruzi strains in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data.

claim: Treatments as long as 60 days often fail to completely clear T. cruzi infection.
source: While these experiments demonstrate that BZN treatment rapidly reduces T. cruzi numbers by 10- to 1000-fold over just a few days, we know from previous studies that such short-term treatments, and indeed treatments as long as 60 days, often fail to completely clear T. cruzi infection (Bustamante et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: The vast majority of amastigotes incorporated EdU during a 24 hr period after EdU injection in acutely infected mice.
source: We first established the in vivo EdU labeling protocol in acutely infected mice with high tissue parasite load, finding that the vast majority of amastigotes incorporated EdU during a 24 hr period after EdU injection (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Most intracellular amastigotes incorporated EdU over 24–72 hr of exposure in chronically infected mice.
source: We then applied this protocol to mice with established chronic T. cruzi infections and again found that most intracellular amastigotes incorporated EdU over the 24–72 hr of exposure.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2 and supplements.

claim: A small fraction of intracellular amastigotes failed to show evidence of replication over 72 hr after EdU injection in chronically infected mice.
source: However a small fraction of intracellular amastigotes failed to show evidence of replication over the 72 hr after EdU injection (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Non-replicating amastigotes were within host cells in which other amastigotes were clearly replicating.
source: Interestingly, these apparently non-replicating amastigotes were within host cells in which the other amastigotes were clearly replicating, suggesting that there is a heterogeneity of amastigotes in infected cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by microscopy data in Figure 2.

claim: Heterogeneity in replication appears to establish within host cells from a single infecting parasite.
source: Since the low parasite load in chronically infected mice makes it highly unlikely that a single host cell is infected by more than one trypomastigote, this heterogeneity in replication appears to establish within host cells from a single infecting parasite Figure 2.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference based on the low parasite load in chronic infection.

claim: A small fraction of amastigotes in host cells in vitro consistently failed to take up EdU, even when exposed for up to 72 hr of the ~96 hr intracellular replication phase.
source: As in the in vivo infection, a small fraction of amastigotes in host cells in vitro consistently failed to take up EdU, even when exposed for up to 72 hr of the ~96 hr intracellular replication phase (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: Apoptosis of amastigotes in host cells is extremely rare.
source: However monitoring for apoptosis of amastigotes in host cells revealed this process to be extremely rare (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by TUNEL assay data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Incorporation of EdU into DNA can impact DNA replication and cell division.
source: Incorporation of EdU into DNA can impact DNA replication and thus cell division (Zhao et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: Replicating amastigotes dilute CFSE and CellTrace Violet dyes, while a fraction of amastigotes remain dye positive.
source: T. cruzi trypomastigotes uniformly stain with either dye and upon infection of host cells, replicating amastigotes dilute the dye, while a fraction of amastigotes remain dye positive, indicating again the limited replication of a subset of amastigotes (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Amastigotes remaining dye positive after 72–96 hr were also EdU-negative.
source: Amastigotes remaining dye positive after 72–96 hr were also EdU-negative (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4C.

claim: Amastigotes that had failed to incorporate EdU during the final ~72 hr in host cells were fully competent to convert to trypomastigotes and to exit host cells.
source: By continuing to monitor infected host cells over time, we observed that amastigotes that had failed to incorporate EdU during the final ~72 hr in host cells were fully competent to convert to trypomastigotes and to exit host cells, along with the previously replicating (EdU+) trypomastigotes (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4D and E.

claim: Trypomastigotes from minimally replicating amastigotes can infect new host cells and re-convert to amastigotes.
source: Not only could trypomastigotes from minimally replicating amastigotes infect new host cells, re-convert to amastigotes (Figure 5A), and begin a new round of replication, but progeny of this replication can also stop dividing soon after invasion and retain dye for >6 days while other progeny of this dormant amastigote divided extensively (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 5A and B.

claim: Progeny of minimally replicating amastigotes can stop dividing soon after invasion and retain dye for >6 days while other progeny divide extensively.
source: Not only could trypomastigotes from minimally replicating amastigotes infect new host cells, re-convert to amastigotes (Figure 5A), and begin a new round of replication, but progeny of this replication can also stop dividing soon after invasion and retain dye for >6 days while other progeny of this dormant amastigote divided extensively (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 5B.

claim: A small proportion of T. cruzi amastigotes halt replication within 24 hr after host cell entry.
source: Thus, a small proportion of T. cruzi amastigotes halt replication within 24 hr after host cell entry but can convert to trypomastigotes that are infection-competent and able to repeat the processes of replication and arrested replication in new host cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: Non-dividing amastigotes are similar in size to recently divided amastigotes.
source: These videos also indicate other characteristics of non-dividing amastigotes that were apparent in other still images, for example that non-dividing amastigotes are similar in size to recently divided amastigotes and are generally Tdtomato-dim, expressing low levels of the Tdtomato fluorescent protein relative to rapidly dividing amastigotes.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on observations from time-lapse videos.

claim: Non-dividing amastigotes are generally Tdtomato-dim, expressing low levels of the Tdtomato fluorescent protein relative to rapidly dividing amastigotes.
source: These videos also indicate other characteristics of non-dividing amastigotes that were apparent in other still images, for example that non-dividing amastigotes are similar in size to recently divided amastigotes and are generally Tdtomato-dim, expressing low levels of the Tdtomato fluorescent protein relative to rapidly dividing amastigotes.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on observations from time-lapse videos.

claim: In BZN-treated mice, the only parasites detected were brightly violet and present at 1 and occasionally two per infected cell.
source: Remarkably, in the BZN-treated mice, the only parasites detected were brightly violet and present at 1 and occasionally two per infected cell (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Actively replicating parasites (violet-negative) were not detected in BZN-treated mice.
source: Actively replicating parasites (violet-negative) were not detected in the BZN-treated mice while a much larger number of violet-negative and less abundant violet-positive parasites were observed in the non-treated mice.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: A resumption of parasite replication was evident in treated mice 9 days after the last of the 2 BNZ treatment doses.
source: A resumption of parasite replication was evident in treated mice 9 days after the last of the 2 BNZ treatment doses, demonstrating that dormant, and therefore drug resistant amastigotes, could also resume division in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: Non-replicating amastigotes developing in interferon-gamma deficient mice survive a minimum of 20 days of BZN treatment.
source: Non-replicating amastigotes developing in these mice survive a minimum of 20 days of BZN treatment (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A) and again resume replication upon cessation of BZN treatment (Figure 6C) and eventually spread extensively in these animals (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Non-replicating amastigotes resume replication upon cessation of BZN treatment in interferon-gamma deficient mice.
source: Non-replicating amastigotes developing in these mice survive a minimum of 20 days of BZN treatment (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A) and again resume replication upon cessation of BZN treatment (Figure 6C) and eventually spread extensively in these animals (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6C.

claim: Parasites can rebound and begin replication after BZN is removed, even following 30 days of high dose BZN treatment in vitro.
source: In all cases, even following 30 days of high dose BZN treatment, parasites can rebound and begin replication after BZN is removed.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: Low numbers of parasites with a range of violet dye retention are evident in cultures during drug treatment.
source: This rebound can often be observed in the whole well Tdtomato fluorescence readings (Figure 7A), and in all cases, low numbers of parasites with a range of violet dye retention are evident in cultures during drug treatment (Figure 7B), as well as resumption of low level to vigorous replication after drug washout (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 7B.

claim: T. cruzi lines rebounding after 30 days of in vitro exposure to BZN had not developed stable resistance to the compound.
source: Further, T. cruzi lines rebounding after 30 days of in vitro exposure to BZN had not developed stable resistance to the compound as the IC50 of BZN on this population remained unchanged from that of the pre-exposed population (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: T. cruzi amastigotes regularly and spontaneously cease replication.
source: Thus, T. cruzi amastigotes regularly and spontaneously cease replication and in that dormant state are resistant to otherwise highly effective trypanocidal drugs for extended periods of time.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental findings.

claim: Dormant T. cruzi amastigotes are resistant to otherwise highly effective trypanocidal drugs for extended periods of time.
source: Thus, T. cruzi amastigotes regularly and spontaneously cease replication and in that dormant state are resistant to otherwise highly effective trypanocidal drugs for extended periods of time.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental findings.

claim: Dormant parasites are capable of re-initiating replication after >30 days of drug exposure.
source: These dormant parasites are capable of re-initiating replication after >30 days of drug exposure and perhaps much longer after the initiation of dormancy.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on the experimental findings.

claim: T. cruzi infection is one of the highest impact infectious disease in the Americas, including in the United States.
source: Although T. cruzi infection is one of the highest impact infectious disease in the Americas, including in the United States, effective prevention, control and treatment methods are virtually non-existent.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as background information.

claim: Effective prevention, control and treatment methods for T. cruzi infection are virtually non-existent.
source: Although T. cruzi infection is one of the highest impact infectious disease in the Americas, including in the United States, effective prevention, control and treatment methods are virtually non-existent.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as background information.

claim: BZN and NFX have been in use for decades.
source: However, although BZN and NFX have been in use for decades, have relatively clear mechanisms of action and do not appear to readily encourage development of genetic-based drug resistance, their unpredictable treatment outcome coupled with their modest to severe side effects has limited their use primarily to acute, childhood, or immunosuppression-exacerbated infections.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as background information.

claim: BZN and NFX have relatively clear mechanisms of action.
source: However, although BZN and NFX have been in use for decades, have relatively clear mechanisms of action and do not appear to readily encourage development of genetic-based drug resistance, their unpredictable treatment outcome coupled with their modest to severe side effects has limited their use primarily to acute, childhood, or immunosuppression-exacerbated infections.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as background information.

claim: BZN and NFX do not appear to readily encourage development of genetic-based drug resistance.
source: However, although BZN and NFX have been in use for decades, have relatively clear mechanisms of action and do not appear to readily encourage development of genetic-based drug resistance, their unpredictable treatment outcome coupled with their modest to severe side effects has limited their use primarily to acute, childhood, or immunosuppression-exacerbated infections.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as background information.

claim: Human clinical trials of new therapies judged to be promising based upon limited studies in experimental models have been colossal failures.
source: Furthermore, human clinical trials of new therapies judged to be promising based upon limited studies in experimental models have been colossal failures (Molina et al., 2014; STOP-CHAGAS Investigators et al., 2017) and ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers NCT01489228, NCT02498782, and NCT01162967), demonstrating these compounds to be clearly inferior to BNZ and NFX.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Parasite strain variation with respect to BZN susceptibility in vivo does not appear to be due to direct resistance to the trypanocidal activity of BZN.
source: Although there is parasite strain variation with respect to BZN susceptibility in vivo, this variation does not appear to be due to direct resistance to the trypanocidal activity of BZN (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: Parasite lines obtained from failed drug treatments are no more resistant to BZN than the pre-treatment parasites.
source: Parasite lines obtained from failed drug treatments are no more resistant to BZN than the pre-treatment parasites (Sup Figure 7), and although BZN resistance can be induced by drug selection in vitro, such partially resistant lines are crippled with respect to initiating and maintaining an infection (Mejia et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Supplementary Figure 7 (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).

claim: BZN resistance can be induced by drug selection in vitro, but such partially resistant lines are crippled with respect to initiating and maintaining an infection.
source: Parasite lines obtained from failed drug treatments are no more resistant to BZN than the pre-treatment parasites (Sup Figure 7), and although BZN resistance can be induced by drug selection in vitro, such partially resistant lines are crippled with respect to initiating and maintaining an infection (Mejia et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: Resistance to BZN treatment is relative, not complete.
source: Thus resistance to BZN treatment is relative, not complete, is not easily selectable, and is not associated with any specific genetic lineage of T. cruzi nor with host genetics.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion based on the evidence presented.

claim: Resistance to BZN treatment is not easily selectable.
source: Thus resistance to BZN treatment is relative, not complete, is not easily selectable, and is not associated with any specific genetic lineage of T. cruzi nor with host genetics.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion based on the evidence presented.

claim: Resistance to BZN treatment is not associated with any specific genetic lineage of T. cruzi nor with host genetics.
source: Thus resistance to BZN treatment is relative, not complete, is not easily selectable, and is not associated with any specific genetic lineage of T. cruzi nor with host genetics.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion based on the evidence presented.

claim: Dormancy in T. cruzi is key to the failure of current drug treatments.
source: The results of the current study firmly connect drug treatment failure in T. cruzi infection to the presence of a previously unrecognized player in this parasite's life cycle, the transiently dormant amastigote.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a key conclusion of the study.

claim: Dormant amastigotes appear at a consistently detectable frequency and are present in many infected host cells in vitro and in vivo.
source: These dormant amastigotes appear at a consistently detectable frequency and are present in many infected host cells in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Dormancy in T. cruzi occurs spontaneously.
source: Dormancy occurs spontaneously and is often observed soon after host cell infection – as shown by the ability of parasites to retain cell division monitoring dyes through several rounds of host cell invasion and expansion.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Dormancy in T. cruzi is often observed soon after host cell infection.
source: Dormancy occurs spontaneously and is often observed soon after host cell infection – as shown by the ability of parasites to retain cell division monitoring dyes through several rounds of host cell invasion and expansion.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Dormancy in T. cruzi may also occur at other points throughout the 4–5 day replication cycle within host cells.
source: However dormancy may also occur at other points throughout the 4–5 day replication cycle within host cells, as suggested by the presence of multiple EdU-negative amastigotes in heavily infected cells and supported by time lapse imaging of infected cells.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Dormant T. cruzi parasites are not permanently arrested.
source: Importantly, these dormant parasites are not permanently arrested, as they resume replication days to weeks after entering dormancy (Figure 7).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: Dormant amastigotes readily respond to the cues that drive conversion to trypomastigote forms within host cells.
source: These dormant amastigotes also readily respond to the cues that drive conversion to trypomastigote forms within host cells, a process that appears to occur only when the host cell is nearly bursting with amastigotes.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Stage conversion from amastigote to trypomastigote appears to occur only when the host cell is nearly bursting with amastigotes.
source: These dormant amastigotes also readily respond to the cues that drive conversion to trypomastigote forms within host cells, a process that appears to occur only when the host cell is nearly bursting with amastigotes.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an observation from the study.

claim: An extremely rare outcome for amastigotes in host cells is death.
source: An extremely rare outcome for amastigotes in host cells is death, as determined by the paucity of degrading amastigotes detected in host cells (Sup Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Supplementary Figure 3 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).

claim: Dormancy is well-studied in bacteria and plays a critical role in their adaptation to changing environments.
source: Dormancy is well-studied in bacteria and plays a critical role in their adaptation to changing environments.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as background information.

claim: Extended dormancy in T. cruzi had been missed by previous investigations likely because it is relatively rare.
source: This phenomenon had been missed by previous investigations in T. cruzi likely because extended dormancy (which would be required to survive during weeks of drug treatment) is relatively rare.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an explanation for why dormancy was not previously recognized.

claim: In vitro studies often report very high efficiency of drugs such as BZN to kill >99% of T. cruzi amastigotes.
source: In vitro studies often report very high efficiency of drugs such as BZN to kill >99% of T. cruzi amastigotes – and the assumption has been that this was in fact 100% killing (Moraes et al., 2014), but this is clearly not the case.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: This is the first report of extended dormancy in an otherwise replicating stage of any trypanosomatid.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first report of extended dormancy in an otherwise replicating stage of any trypanosomatid.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: Leishmania sp intracellular amastigotes exhibit greatly reduced proliferation and metabolism relative to the extracellular promastigote forms.
